newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aegon wins licence in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Aegon wins licence in Philippines.

text.p: Aegon NV said on Thursday it won a licence to start life insurance business in the Philippines.

The group, which had previously announced it sought expansion in the Far East, has set up a unit called Aegon Life Insurance (Philippines) Inc, which will start with a shareholder equity of about 21 million guilders.
"Having this licence gives the (Aegon) group an even better position in talks about possible cooperation pacts," the Dutch insurer said in a statement.
The new unit is expected to start operations by the end of 1997 and will be gradually developed.
Aegon said it aimed at gaining an important position in the Asian market in the next 10 years by setting up new activities, which will be led by experienced local managers.

Aegon entered the Asian market in 1993 when it opened an office in Taiwan. Earlier this year it took a 30 percent stake in portfolio manager Clemente Holdings Ltd which is active in the Philippines through an investment fund and a mutual fund management company.
Aegon said the market for life insurance in the Philippines generated a total premium income of about 750 million guilders in 1994.
This was rather small compared with other Asian countries but the growth potential could be compared with other Asian emerging markets, it added.
Aegon posted 1995 net profit of 1.3 billion guilders on group turnover of 21 billion.
